faqItems.a: JPEG, WebP and AVIF are lossy: a lower quality value means a smaller file but more visible artifacts. PNG uses lossless optimization by default and loses no quality.

faqItems.q: What quality value should I use?
faqItems.a: 75–85 is a good default for sharing, 60–80 for the web. If you need strict fidelity, enable lossless (PNG) or go above 90.
It controls how hard the AVIF encoder searches. Higher values compress more thoroughly and produce smaller files, but take longer. It does not affect quality.

faqItems.q: How large can files be? Can I batch?
faqItems.a: You can add many images at once and they are processed automatically in sequence. Larger files use more memory, so keep a single batch within a few hundred MB.
Results live only in browser memory. Download them individually or use "Download all". Refreshing the page discards them.

faqItems.q: Which formats can I convert between?
faqItems.a: JPEG, PNG, WebP and AVIF in any direction. Files already in the target format are skipped.

faqItems.q: Will converting to PNG make my file smaller or larger?
faqItems.a: PNG is lossless, so it is usually larger than JPEG or WebP. Choose it when you need transparency or a lossless copy.
AVIF compresses better and produces smaller files, but encodes slower and has weaker support in older browsers. WebP is the safer default.

faqItems.q: Can I extract a frame from a video?
faqItems.a: No. This tool only handles still images. To extract audio from a video, use the Audio Transcoding page.
Converting to WebP, AVIF or PNG keeps the alpha channel. Converting to JPEG fills transparent areas with a solid color.

faqItems.q: Why doesn't this work on mobile?
faqItems.a: Video transcoding needs a lot of memory and CPU. Mobile browsers tend to crash with out-of-memory errors, so the feature is desktop only.
H.265 gives smaller files at the same quality but encodes slower and won't play on some older devices. Pick H.264 for maximum compatibility.
18–28 is the useful range. Lower means better quality and a larger file. Around 23 suits most content.
Everything runs in your browser through WebAssembly. Speed depends on your CPU, the resolution and the length of the video. Keep this tab in the foreground and let it finish.

faqItems.q: Can I remove the audio track?
faqItems.a: Yes. Enable "Remove audio" to export a silent video.

faqItems.q: What kind of image should I upload?
faqItems.a: A square image such as 512×512. Non-square images are cropped or padded, which distorts the icon.
Selecting all is usually right. 16×16 and 32×32 are for browser tabs, 180×180 for Apple Touch icons, and 192×192 plus 512×512 for PWA.
favicon.ico is the traditional format understood by browsers and Windows shortcuts; PNG suits modern browsers and PWA. Download both.

faqItems.q: How do I use the generated files?
faqItems.a: Put them in your site root and add the matching <link rel="icon"> tags to your <head>.
Yes. Upload a PNG or SVG with an alpha channel and the generated icons keep the transparent areas.

faqItems.a: MP3, AAC, M4A, OGG, FLAC and WAV, convertible in any direction.

faqItems.q: Can I extract audio from a video?
faqItems.a: Yes. Upload an MP4, WebM, MOV or AVI file directly and pick an output format; only the audio track is kept.
192–320 kbps for music, 96–128 kbps is fine for speech. Higher means better quality and a larger file.

faqItems.q: Does converting to FLAC improve quality?
faqItems.a: No. FLAC is lossless, so it preserves the source exactly. Converting a lossy file to FLAC makes it larger without improving quality.
Usually yes. It keeps the original sample rate and avoids an unnecessary resampling step.
